display.title: Episode 138: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak's Brachah of Joy (Shabbos Mevarchim Elul)
display.summary_short: Why should a Jew be happy? Uncle Yossi tells how Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev 'skipped' a morning brachah out of sheer joy, plus a guest folk song and Shabbos Mevarchim Elul.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with Dovid HaMelech's call to serve Hashem with joy and asks where real happiness comes from. He answers with a story: one morning Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev led the morning brachos in shul and seemed to leave out the brachah thanking Hashem for making us Jewish. After davening the worried congregants asked why. The tzaddik explained that while saying Modeh Ani he was so overwhelmed by the thought that his Jewish soul is truly a part of Hashem that he jumped up and said that brachah right away at home. The lesson: being a Yid is reason enough to be happy all day. After the Hakochainik march and a word from the sponsor, a fifth-grade boy from a Crown Heights yeshiva leads the Shema. Two guest musicians perform a sing-along folk song about the Land of Israel belonging to every Jew since Avraham. The show closes with mazel tov wishes to a listening family, a reminder that this Shabbos blesses the month of Elul ahead of the new year 5745, and the Dial-a-Jewish-Story number.
display.lesson: You don't have to look far for a reason to be happy: your Jewish soul is a part of Hashem, so serve Hashem with joy all day.

date.note: On air: 'this coming Shabbos is Shabbos Mevarchim Chodesh Elul' and the coming year is 5745 (Shin-Mem-Hei). Shabbos Mevarchim Elul 5744 = 25 Aug 1984, so the Tuesday broadcast is 21 Aug 1984.
